html:
The Colossus of Rhodes was a huge bronze statue of the sun god Helios, the patron of the island city of Rhodes. It was finished around 280 BCE and stood about 33 metres tall, making it one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

The Rhodians built it to celebrate surviving the siege of Rhodes in 305 and 304 BCE, and paid for it partly by selling the siege machines that Demetrius left behind. The sculptor Chares of Lindos took about twelve years to make it, with bronze plates over an iron frame weighted with stones.

It stood for only about 54 years. An earthquake in 226 BCE snapped it at the knees and threw it down. An oracle warned the Rhodians not to rebuild it, so the pieces lay on the ground for centuries, still drawing visitors. The popular picture of the Colossus standing astride the harbour mouth is a later myth.

Its fame lasted. The Statue of Liberty was called "the New Colossus" in the poem on its base. Like the Lighthouse of Alexandria, built in the same years, it showed off the wealth of the new Hellenistic world.
sum: The Colossus of Rhodes was a huge bronze statue of the sun god Helios, the patron of the island city of Rhodes. It was finished around 280 BCE and stood about 33 metres tall, making it one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
